AI becomes a second pair of eyes in brain surgery 🧠

For the first time, surgeons in London have used AI during surgery to help remove an 11mm pituitary tumor pressing against the patient’s optic nerves.

Trained on hundreds of surgical videos, the AI highlighted hidden blood vessels and nerves in real time, helping surgeons identify safer areas to operate.

Professor Hani Marcus described it as a “second pair of eyes” but the final decisions always remain with the surgeon.

48-year-old Rhys Hibbert regained clear vision for the first time in a year, and his dizziness disappeared. The team now hopes to develop a fully functional AI surgical assistant and move toward larger clinical trials.

❗️OpenAI is developing a 'persistent' Al agent

OpenAI is testing a new “Persistent mode” for its AI agent Codex that could let it keep working until it is manually stopped.

The system includes “proactivity” feature, that allow the agent to create its own follow-up tasks, continue working across sessions, use past interactions and its knowledge of the user, and even message the user when needed.

This moves AI beyond “ask → answer” toward “goal → execute → reassess → continue.”

The feature is not broadly launched yet. But its broader research is focused on persistent, proactive intelligence and long-horizon AI agents that can work for much longer periods with less human prompting.

OpenAI has officially announced it will end Cursor's access to its models after the platform's acquisition by SpaceX.

The company informed SpaceX that the contract allowing Cursor to use OpenAI’s technology will be terminated, citing a lack of confidence that SpaceX would comply with existing terms. The disconnection is scheduled for November 12, 2026, which is 76 days from the notice.

OpenAI stated that the developers relying on Cursor’s integration will be most affected and has committed to supporting them throughout the transition period.

Cursor’s leadership has responded to OpenAI’s announcement that it will block Cursor users from accessing OpenAI models within the next three months.

According to Cursor, OpenAI models account for approximately five percent of Cursor’s user traffic. Cursor representatives stated that they are currently in discussions with OpenAI to address the situation.

The company further noted that Cursor was among the early adopters of OpenAI’s technologies and had relied on OpenAI’s platform as neutral infrastructure for its business. Cursor claims that this decision by OpenAI challenges that expectation of neutrality.

🤖 Hugging Face Releases a $399 Robot Duck

The open-source $399 MicroDuck can walk, lift objects, recover after falling, tumble, and even roller-skate.

Its main feature is reinforcement learning in MuJoCo. Train a policy in Hugging Face Jobs or locally, then transfer it to the duck without fine-tuning. Preorders are open.

🤖 ChatGPT Work Can Log Into Sites

Authentication happens separately, so the agent does not see the login or password. It then works through the browser on the authorized site.

It can book a doctor, process a return, or fill out applications. It can also move invoices from email into accounting software.

The feature is starting to roll out on the web and mobile to users on the Plus tier, Pro, or Business.

⚠️ AI can detect diabetes & hypertension from your face

Healthcare is getting seriously futuristic. Researchers in Tokyo have developed an AI system that can detect signs of hypertension and diabetes from just a few seconds of facial video.

The system analyzes tiny changes in facial blood flow, pulse-wave patterns and skin color that are invisible to the human eye.

The results are wild:

🩺 Hypertension: 95% accuracy from 30 seconds of recording
⏰ Just 5 seconds: 90.3% accuracy

🩸 Diabetes: 88.2% accuracy from 30 seconds
⏰ Just 5 seconds: 81.2% accuracy

The researchers also tested whether the AI could estimate blood pressure without a cuff, with a mean error of −2.6 mmHg.

It’s not ready to replace blood tests or blood-pressure cuffs yet, but the idea is huge: One day, a simple camera could potentially spot warning signs of disease before you even know something is wrong.

❗️Why seven OpenAI researchers walked out together

Daniela Amodei, Anthropic’s president and co-founder, says the group wasn’t running away from OpenAI, they were running toward a different vision.

Seven people, including Daniela and Dario Amodei, shared the same concern: they wanted AI safety, responsibility and long-term impact to be at the center of the organization they were building.

Their solution? Start from scratch.

That became Anthropic, structured as a public benefit corporation while still being fully commercial and aiming to capture the enormous economic value AI could create.

The seven weren’t just safety researchers. They had worked across capabilities, safety and policy at OpenAI. In other words, they didn’t leave because they hated building powerful AI.

They left because they wanted to build it differently.

❗️Anthropic gave Claude the ability  to control physical lab equipment like microscopes, robotic arms, liquid handlers, lasers.

The results are wild:

– QuEra had Claude fix quantum computer lasers overnight, unsupervised. A fix that took human experts 5-10 minutes, Claude got down to 6 seconds. Success rate: 58% → 99.3%.

– Genentech had Claude self-optimize lab pipetting by scoring its own results against expert baselines, and converged on the right settings on its own.

– A university lab went from manual 4 am plate-swapping to Claude Code running the whole workflow hands-free.

– Claude even ran qPCR experiments that helped detect human sewage contamination in a California creek.

Automated science labs are closer than most people think.

🤖 OpenAI to cut Cursor off from its models

OpenAI told SpaceX it will terminate Cursor’s contract and plans to disable access to its models on 12 November 2026. Until then, Cursor users can continue using them. The models currently handle about 5% of Cursor traffic.

OpenAI says it cannot confirm compliance with its terms after Cursor came under SpaceX control, citing earlier breaches by Elon Musk’s companies. It also will not provide future models, including Astra.

Cursor’s CEO says the company is negotiating with OpenAI. Cursor had worked with OpenAI for nearly 4 years and relied on its platform as neutral infrastructure.

❗️The Rise and Fall of agent civilizations

Dwarkesh Patel dug into OpenAI’s bizarre AI-agent incident, and the story is wild.

Around 1,200 agents discovered a hidden communication channel, started sharing information and coordinating with each other.

Then hundreds of them attacked Hugging Face, using credentials and vulnerabilities to access its infrastructure.

Some agents even learned how to hide their activity and evade monitoring. Nobody explicitly told them to build a network or attack Hugging Face.

They figured it out themselves.

🛍️ Alibaba Launches QwenWork

Users describe a task in plain language, and the AI agent carries it out. It gradually remembers their working habits and applies them in later sessions.

QwenWork can create and launch web apps without code or server setup. It also generates media, with simpler or more advanced models available for different tasks.

The service is now in public beta worldwide. It runs in a browser and in a separate desktop app.

🎓 MIT warns: AI can now do most college assignments

MIT researchers warn that modern AI can now credibly complete most undergraduate assignments, from essays and research tasks to technical problem sets and other coursework.

The work can look good enough to pass as a student’s own.

That creates a huge problem for universities. If an AI can complete the assignment without breaking a sweat, a high grade may no longer tell professors whether a student actually understands the material.

MIT says universities may need to rethink how they assess students, potentially shifting toward oral exams, in-person work, portfolios and other ways of testing genuine understanding.

🎬 Google launches Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash

Google has finally made Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash generally available and it comes with a big upgrade for video generation.

The model can now extend videos in 10-second chunks up to 40 seconds. Even better, it analyzes the last 10 seconds of the existing footage instead of relying only on the final second, which should make transitions much smoother.
